facts.text: Dancyville was named after blacksmith Isaac Dancy who arrived in early 1831.
The first Dancyville United Methodist Church was founded in 1837, followed by a Baptist church in 1838 that no longer exists, and a Presbyterian church in 1853.
During the Civil War, two companies formed in Dancyville: the Dancyville Grays and Company L of the 9th Tennessee Infantry.
The 140‑year‑old Temple Adas Israel in Dancyville is the oldest Jewish synagogue in Tennessee still holding services.
Dancyville sits at the crossroads of State Routes 76 and 179, just north of Interstate 40, at latitude 35.408 and longitude –89.294.
In 1849 the Dancyville Female Academy opened in the local Masonic Lodge, later becoming part of the town’s educational heritage.
